INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #11 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does pronunciation mean? (1 mark)
   A. The meaning of a word
   B. The length of a story
   C. The way we say the sounds of words
   D. The way we write words

2. Why should you not translate a saying from your language word for word? (1 mark)
   A. The meaning may be lost
   B. It is always easy
   C. It is against the law
   D. Words are never important

3. What is a level reader? (1 mark)
   A. A tool for measuring floors
   B. A type of dictionary
   C. A book written for a particular reading level
   D. A machine

4. What does the Kiswahili proverb Haba na haba hujaza kibaba teach? (1 mark)
   A. Big things are useless
   B. Never save
   C. Small amounts added together become a lot
   D. Only large amounts count

5. What does a peer review checklist help with? (1 mark)
   A. Checking a partner's story kindly
   B. Stealing ideas
   C. Ending the lesson
   D. Cleaning the room

6. How should a proverb be used in a composition? (1 mark)
   A. With no meaning
   B. Anywhere at all
   C. Only at the start
   D. In a way that fits the story

7. How should you speak when narrating an event? (1 mark)
   A. Very quietly
   B. Clearly and with feeling
   C. Angrily always
   D. Without stopping

8. Which of these should you include when describing an event? (1 mark)
   A. Only the date
   B. Only the name
   C. Who, where, when, what happened and how you felt
   D. Nothing

9. What is a conman? (1 mark)
   A. A shopkeeper
   B. A teacher
   C. A farmer
   D. A person who tricks people to get money

10. Why do we check a dictionary meaning against the sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Words can have more than one meaning
   B. Words never change
   C. Sentences have no meaning
   D. Dictionaries are wrong

11. What is a receipt? (1 mark)
   A. A type of fruit
   B. A kind of coin
   C. A paper that shows you paid
   D. A shop

12. What is a bargain? (1 mark)
   A. To steal
   B. To discuss the price
   C. To run
   D. To sleep

13. What is a mosaic? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of song
   B. A long story
   C. A heavy load
   D. A picture made of small pieces

14. Which word means not inside? (1 mark)
   A. beside
   B. under
   C. outside
   D. between

15. What is a refrain? (1 mark)
   A. A rhyme only
   B. A page
   C. A line that is repeated
   D. The title

16. What is spoken word? (1 mark)
   A. A silent song
   B. A kind of drawing
   C. Poetry performed aloud for an audience
   D. A dictionary

17. Why should you mark pauses in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. To hide words
   B. To make it longer
   C. To know where to stop and breathe
   D. To spoil the page

18. What is the meaning of reciting a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Saying it aloud, usually from memory
   B. Writing it
   C. Erasing it
   D. Copying it

19. Which of these is a character? (1 mark)
   A. A cloudy afternoon
   B. A girl called Neema
   C. Under the tree
   D. The last page

20. Which starting sentence would make a reader curious? (1 mark)
   A. One cloudy afternoon, Neema saw a thin dog under a tree.
   B. The end.
   C. Yes.
   D. Page one.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Mama Neema buys a box of bananas for 200 shillings and sells it for 260 shillings. Find her profit. (2 marks)

22. Write a paragraph of four sentences about a time you handled money. Use when at least twice. (5 marks)

23. State three benefits of reading widely. (3 marks)

24. Plan a short oral narrative about a school rule. Say the characters, the events, the ending, and where you will use a simile and a metaphor. (5 marks)

25. A picture shows a girl beside a thin dog under a tree with an empty bowl. Write a story plan and a four-sentence story. (5 marks)

26. Divide into subject and predicate: My brother saves coins. (2 marks)

27. Name two prepositions used to show position. (2 marks)

28. Describe how to mark a line of a poem for reading aloud. (4 marks)

29. Give two conjunctions used to join sentences. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #11 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — The way we say the sounds of words
   Pronunciation is how words are said.

2. A — The meaning may be lost
   Sayings often carry meaning beyond the words.

3. C — A book written for a particular reading level
   Level readers match the skills of the pupils.

4. C — Small amounts added together become a lot
   The proverb means little by little fills the measure.

5. A — Checking a partner's story kindly
   Peer review helps improve writing.

6. D — In a way that fits the story
   A proverb should match the lesson of the story.

7. B — Clearly and with feeling
   Clear speech and feeling make a story good.

8. C — Who, where, when, what happened and how you felt
   These details make the event clear.

9. D — A person who tricks people to get money
   A conman deceives others.

10. A — Words can have more than one meaning
   The right meaning depends on context.

11. C — A paper that shows you paid
   A receipt is proof of payment.

12. B — To discuss the price
   Bargaining is agreeing on price.

13. D — A picture made of small pieces
   A mosaic is made of small pieces of paper or seeds.

14. C — outside
   Outside means not inside.

15. C — A line that is repeated
   A refrain is repeated in a poem or song.

16. C — Poetry performed aloud for an audience
   Spoken word is performed poetry.

17. C — To know where to stop and breathe
   Pauses help the listener follow.

18. A — Saying it aloud, usually from memory
   To recite is to say aloud.

19. B — A girl called Neema
   Characters are people or animals.

20. A — One cloudy afternoon, Neema saw a thin dog under a tree.
   A specific opening makes the reader want to read on.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: 260 minus 200 equals 60 shillings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the working and one mark for the answer with units.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two uses of when, for example When I reached the shop, I counted my money. When I paid, I received change. I was happy.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear sentence and one mark for correct use of when.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: It builds vocabulary, improves spelling, gives new ideas, makes you a better writer and speaker, gives enjoyment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each benefit.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any plan with characters, events in order, an ending with a lesson, and one simile and one metaphor, for example a pupil who came late but learned that rules are like a map.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, events, ending, simile and metaphor.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: A plan with title, characters, setting, problem and ending, followed by four sentences that show the girl helping the dog and end with a lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, setting and problem, and two marks for a clear four-sentence story.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Subject: My brother. Predicate: saves coins.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: on, in, under, behind, beside, between, in front of, outside (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Underline words to stress, draw a slash where you will pause, read the line using your marks and check that it sounds natural.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: and, but, or, so (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.
